newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks open Indian markets, smaller state role.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks open Indian markets, smaller state role.

text.p: India has the potential for much more business with the United States and should open up its economy, lower the role of the state and attract more investment, a senior U.S. Treasury official said on Saturday.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a meeting here celebrating the 50th anniversary of Indian independence, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers also said that the United States had a strong interest in a stable and prosperous India.
"The challenge for India's second 50 years is to free its economy and its people ... to become, not just the world's largest democracy, but the fastest growing," Summers said.

"Our highest priority in our relations with India is the same as it is in every emerging economy, namely to smooth the way for the U.S. and Indian private sectors to work together in ways which help both our economies," he added.

Summers said state subsidies in India were distorting the economy and thwarting efforts to improve productivity and attract private investment. Would-be investors faced too many rules and regulations and financial markets had to be freed.
"India will not come close to meeting its heaving infrastructure needs without free and efficient financial markets," he said.

He said the liberalization of trade rules would help consumers and small business, while trade and banking sector reforms would be needed to ensure that plans to lift capital controls were successful.
